title: The Most Important Supreme Court Term in Decades

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的那个黑胶唱片时代，你每天晚上都要带300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Estet Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的埃斯特·赫恩登。

sentences.en: In for Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 代班迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the Supreme Court will soon take on some of the country's most controversial topics, including abortion access and gun rights.
sentences.zh: 今天，最高法院即将审理一些美国最具争议的话题，包括堕胎权和持枪权。

sentences.en: But the high-profile cases come at a time of growing concern over how politicized the court seems to Americans.
sentences.zh: 但这些备受瞩目的案件审理之际，正值美国民众对法院政治化倾向日益担忧之时。

sentences.en: My colleague, Adam Liptak, on the historic upcoming term, and why the court's public perception matters.
sentences.zh: 我的同事亚当·利普塔克将带我们了解即将到来的历史性庭审期，以及为什么公众对法院的看法至关重要。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月5日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hey, Adam, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，亚当，你好吗？

sentences.en: Hello, I'm good.
sentences.zh: 你好，我很好。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: It is nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Also, where are you right now?
sentences.zh: 另外，你现在在哪里？

sentences.en: I'm back from the court.
sentences.zh: 我刚从法院回来。

sentences.en: I'm in my home office.
sentences.zh: 我在我的家庭办公室里。

sentences.en: I've taken off my suit.
sentences.zh: 我已经脱掉了西装。

sentences.en: I've put on shorts, and it feels like a normal day again.
sentences.zh: 换上了短裤，感觉又像平常的一天了。

sentences.en: So, you're back from the court.
sentences.zh: 所以，你刚从法院回来。

sentences.en: So, the Supreme Court is back in person.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，最高法院恢复了线下开庭。

sentences.en: What was the court like?
sentences.zh: 法院现场是什么样的？

sentences.en: Oh, yay, oh, yay, oh, yay.
sentences.zh: 哦，肃静，肃静，肃静。

sentences.en: All persons having business before the honorable...
sentences.zh: 所有在尊贵的法庭前有事务要处理的人……

sentences.en: Well, it was really different, because for starters, the public is excluded.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的非常不同，因为首先，公众被拒之门外了。

sentences.en: Only the press is allowed in.
sentences.zh: 只有媒体获准进入。

sentences.en: And whereas we usually sit on a bench to the left side of the courtroom, they scattered us around the public section to have social distancing.
sentences.zh: 而且我们通常坐在法庭左侧的席位上，但为了保持社交距离，他们把我们分散在公众席位上。

sentences.en: They required us to wear N95 masks.
sentences.zh: 他们要求我们佩戴N95口罩。

sentences.en: The justices themselves, though, with one exception, Sonia Sotomayor, were not masked, which might surprise some people, particularly in light of the fact that one justice,
sentences.zh: 不过，大法官们自己——除了索尼娅·索托马约尔之外——都没有戴口罩，这可能会让一些人感到惊讶，特别是考虑到其中一位大法官，

sentences.en: Brett Kavanaugh, was missing, having gotten a positive COVID test back on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 布雷特·卡瓦诺，因为周四新冠检测呈阳性而缺席了。

sentences.en: Justice Kavanaugh will be participating today remotely.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺大法官今天将远程参与庭审。

sentences.en: Did Justin Sotomayor say why she was wearing a mask?
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官有没有说她为什么要戴口罩？

sentences.en: Is it just a personal decision?
sentences.zh: 这只是她个人的决定吗？

sentences.en: She didn't say why.
sentences.zh: 她没有说明原因。

sentences.en: I think it's well known that she has diabetes, and that probably figures into it.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都知道她患有糖尿病，这可能是一个考量因素。

sentences.en: We will hear argument first this morning in original case...
sentences.zh: 今天上午我们首先要听取的是原告案件的辩论……

sentences.en: What cases did they kick off with today?
sentences.zh: 他们今天以什么案件开场？

sentences.en: Mr. Coghlan.
sentences.zh: 科格伦先生。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, may I please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，请允许我向法庭陈述。

sentences.en: So, they kicked off with cases that are characteristic of the court's docket.
sentences.zh: 他们以一些符合法院日常审理特点的案件开场。

sentences.en: It's bread and butter cases.
sentences.zh: 都是些家常便饭般的案件。

sentences.en: One involved sentencing, a kind of three-strikes law, and the other was a water dispute between Mississippi and Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 一个涉及量刑，类似于“三振出局法”，另一个是密西西比州和田纳西州之间的水资源纠纷。

sentences.en: Mississippi is mad that Tennessee is taking a lot of groundwater out of land in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州对田纳西州从其境内抽取大量地下水感到不满。

sentences.en: You know, so that gives you a sense of not the world's most exciting cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，这让你感觉到这些并不是世界上最令人兴奋的案件。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，律师。

sentences.en: The case is submitted.
sentences.zh: 案件已提交。

sentences.en: But they're the bread and butter of the court's work, as I say, and they're leading up to, later in the term, to some real blockbusters.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，这些是法院工作的家常便饭，它们是为庭审期后期的一些重磅案件做铺垫。

sentences.en: Let's dig into those blockbusters.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨一下那些重磅案件。

sentences.en: Where should we start?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Well, the biggest one is definitely abortion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的一个绝对是堕胎问题。

sentences.en: The abortion case involves a Mississippi law.
sentences.zh: 这起堕胎案涉及密西西比州的一项法律。

sentences.en: This is a case that is a direct challenge to Roe v.
sentences.zh: 这是一个直接挑战“罗诉韦德案”的案件，

sentences.en: Wade, which said that before fetal viability, states can't ban abortion.
sentences.zh: 该案裁定在胎儿具备生存能力之前，各州不得禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: Fetal viability these days is about 23 weeks.
sentences.zh: 如今胎儿的生存能力大约在23周左右。

sentences.en: The law in question in Mississippi makes abortions unlawful, most abortions, after 15 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的相关法律规定，怀孕15周后堕胎即为非法，大多数堕胎行为均在此列。

sentences.en: Now, red states pass laws like these all the time, saying we're going to outlaw abortion after 6 weeks or 10 weeks or 12 weeks or 15 weeks.
sentences.zh: 现在，共和党执政的州经常通过这类法律，声称要在6周、10周、12周或15周后禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: And that's been going on for some time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续了一段时间。

sentences.en: And the lower courts routinely strike down these laws because they're in conflict with Supreme Court precedent.
sentences.zh: 下级法院通常会推翻这些法律，因为它们与最高法院的先例相冲突。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court routinely denies review.
sentences.zh: 而最高法院通常会拒绝复审。

sentences.en: And that was what a lot of people expected when Mississippi passed its 15-week law.
sentences.zh: 这也是密西西比州通过其15周禁令时，许多人的预期。

sentences.en: The lower courts struck it down, saying it was a calculated attempt to go after Roe v.
sentences.zh: 下级法院推翻了它，称这是针对“罗诉韦德案”的一次蓄意攻击。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: And then when the Supreme Court was asked to hear the case, it didn't act right away.
sentences.zh: 当最高法院被要求审理此案时，它并没有立即采取行动。

sentences.en: It waited through 10 or a dozen private conferences among the justices.
sentences.zh: 它在法官们的十几次闭门会议中等待着。

sentences.en: Amy Coney Barrett arrives.
sentences.zh: 艾米·科尼·巴雷特到任了。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, the court finally says, we're going to hear the case.
sentences.zh: 结果出人意料，法院最终表示，我们要审理此案。

sentences.en: It feels like my whole life, the prospect, of a case that comes before the court and dismantles Roe v.
sentences.zh: 感觉我这一生中，关于一个案件来到法院并推翻“罗诉韦德案”的前景，

sentences.en: Wade has been talked about as a possibility.
sentences.zh: 一直被当作一种可能性在讨论。

sentences.en: You're saying that this might be the case.
sentences.zh: 你是说这可能就是那个案件。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: How is what we're going to see in that case different or related to what we saw the Supreme Court do in the Texas abortion law case that's been all over the news recently?
sentences.zh: 我们在该案中看到的，与最近新闻中热议的德克萨斯州堕胎法案中最高法院的做法有何不同或联系？

sentences.en: So to hear the majority on the court tell that the two cases are very, very different.
sentences.zh: 听听法院多数派的说法，这两个案件是非常、非常不同的。

sentences.en: Texas enacted a law saying no abortions after six weeks in most cases.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州颁布了一项法律，规定在大多数情况下，怀孕6周后不得堕胎。

sentences.en: And the innovation of the law was the state wasn't going to enforce it.
sentences.zh: 该法律的创新之处在于州政府并不负责执行它。

sentences.en: It was going to be enforced through private people or given incentives to enforce it in private lawsuits.
sentences.zh: 它将通过私人个人来执行，或者通过激励机制鼓励私人诉讼来执行。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court in a five to four decision on September 1st let that law go into effect.
sentences.zh: 9月1日，最高法院以5比4的投票结果允许该法律生效。

sentences.en: But the majority said this was a procedural ruling only, that it wasn't ruling on the constitutionality of that Texas six-week law.
sentences.zh: 但多数派表示，这仅仅是一个程序性裁决，并未对德克萨斯州6周禁令的合宪性做出裁决。

sentences.en: The Mississippi 15-week law is a direct constitutional challenge.
sentences.zh: 而密西西比州的15周禁令是一项直接的宪法挑战。

sentences.en: The court is asked to address, is the law constitutional?
sentences.zh: 法院被要求解决的问题是：该法律是否合宪？

sentences.en: Does the law violate Roe v.
sentences.zh: 该法律是否违反了“罗诉韦德案”？

sentences.en: Wade?
sentences.zh: 韦德案？

sentences.en: So for legal reasons, there's a distinction between the case because one was decided on, as the majority said, procedural reasons,
sentences.zh: 因此，从法律角度来看，这两个案件之间存在区别，因为一个正如多数派所说，是基于程序原因做出的裁决，

sentences.en: why the Mississippi case would be a direct challenge to the substance of Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而密西西比州的案件则是对“罗诉韦德案”实质内容的直接挑战。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: But how likely is it that the court does overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 那么，法院通过密西西比州的案件推翻“罗诉韦德案”的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: Wade with that Mississippi case?
sentences.zh: 我认为有三种基本选择。

sentences.en: I'd say there are three basic choices.
sentences.zh: 第一种是法院可能推翻密西西比州的法律。

sentences.en: The first one is that the court could strike down the Mississippi law.
sentences.zh: 这种情况不太可能发生，因为下级法院已经推翻了该法律。

sentences.en: That's not a particularly likely scenario because the lower courts had already struck down the law.
sentences.zh: 而且不清楚最高法院为什么要受理此案，仅仅是为了重申法院在所有这些案件中长期以来的做法。

sentences.en: And it's not clear why the Supreme Court would take the case just to reaffirm what courts have been doing for a long time in all these cases.
sentences.zh: 第二种选择是法院维持密西西比州的法律，支持它，但声称这并不从根本上推翻“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: The second option is for the court to sustain the Mississippi law, to uphold it, but to say it's not fundamentally overruling Roe v.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 它在做一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: It's doing something different.
sentences.zh: 现在，“罗诉韦德案”的核心在于，它规定各州不得在胎儿具备生存能力之前禁止堕胎，正如我所说，这大约是23周。

sentences.en: Now, Roe v.
sentences.zh: 所以，很难将“罗诉韦德案”与一项规定15周的法律调和起来。

sentences.en: Wade, at its core, says states can't ban abortions before viability, which, you know, as I've said, is about 23 weeks.
sentences.zh: 但法院可以借鉴早期的案例，声称我们没有推翻“罗诉韦德案”，我们只是在修订它，在修补它。

sentences.en: So it's very hard to reconcile Roe with a law that says 15 weeks.
sentences.zh: 它可以利用早期案例中的一些措辞，比如“过度负担”和“实质性障碍”，并说，听着，15周，大多数女性仍然可以堕胎。

sentences.en: But the court could draw on earlier cases and say, we're not overruling Roe, we're just revising it, we're tinkering with it.
sentences.zh: 15周并没有施加过度负担，也没有构成实质性障碍。

sentences.en: And it could use some language from earlier cases like undue burden and substantial obstacle and say, listen, 15 weeks, most women can still get abortions.
sentences.zh: 我们没有推翻“罗诉韦德案”，但我们要维持密西西比州的法律。

sentences.en: 15 weeks doesn't impose an undue burden, doesn't present a substantial obstacle.
sentences.zh: 然后是第三种选择，也是对法院中最保守的成员有吸引力的选择，即引发头条新闻的那种，你知道，

sentences.en: And we're not overruling Roe, but we're going to sustain the Mississippi law.
sentences.zh: 最高法院推翻“罗诉韦德案”，那将是一个重大的新闻日。

sentences.en: And then the third option, and an option that will be, you know, attractive to the most conservative members of the court, is the one that gives rise to the headline, you know,
sentences.zh: 第三种选择就是直接推翻先例。

sentences.en: Supreme Court overturns Roe v.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Wade, which would be a big news day.
sentences.zh: 那么这些结果对美国更广泛的堕胎权意味着什么？

sentences.en: The third option is just a direct reversal of the precedent.
sentences.zh: 当你谈到部分推翻和完全推翻之间的区别时，这在人们获得堕胎服务的机会或能力方面意味着什么？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 15周的限制会对一些女性造成困难。

sentences.en: So what do these outcomes potentially mean for abortion access in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但大多数女性在15周前就进行了堕胎。

sentences.en: more broadly?
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是想淡化这一点，但密西西比州唯一提供堕胎服务的诊所只做到16周。

sentences.en: When you talk about the difference between a partial reversal and a full reversal, what does that mean in terms of people's access or ability to get abortions?
sentences.zh: 所以15周将是一个相对温和的削减。

sentences.en: So 15 weeks would impose a hardship on some women.
sentences.zh: 但如果法院完全推翻“罗诉韦德案”，那些共和党执政的州已经准备好了。

sentences.en: But most women get abortions before 15 weeks.
sentences.zh: 大约有10个州有所谓的“触发法”，如果“罗诉韦德案”被推翻，堕胎将立即成为非法。

sentences.en: So I don't mean to minimize this at all, but the only clinic in Mississippi offering abortions only does it to 16 weeks.
sentences.zh: 我们的报道显示，在短时间内，大约22个州将使堕胎成为非法，这将是美国生活的一次巨变。

sentences.en: So 15 weeks would be a relatively modest cutback.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: But if the court were to overrule Roe entirely, the red states are ready to go.
sentences.zh: 所以已经有10个州准备好了法律，一旦“罗诉韦德案”被推翻，就立即取缔堕胎服务。

sentences.en: About 10 of them have so-called trigger laws, which would make abortion unlawful immediately if Roe is overturned.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And our reporting suggests that in short order, about 22 states would make abortion unlawful, which would be a sea change in American life.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是已经颁布的法律，只是在等待这个前提条件。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一旦法院推翻“罗诉韦德案”，我们就会让堕胎成为非法。

sentences.en: So 10 states already have laws ready if Roe is overturned to immediately outlaw abortion access.
sentences.zh: 所以我们本庭审期有一个潜在的非常激进的堕胎案件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但这还不是全部。

sentences.en: So these are enacted laws that are just waiting for this predicate.
sentences.zh: 法院将重新审视宪法第二修正案。

sentences.en: You know, once the court overrules Roe, we're going to make abortion unlawful.
sentences.zh: 那起第二修正案案件是什么？

sentences.en: So we have a potentially quite radical abortion case on the docket this term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，法院在2008年和2010年做出两项裁决，首次确立了个人拥有枪支的权利后，就该问题一直保持沉默。

sentences.en: But that's not all.
sentences.zh: 实际上，法院到目前为止告诉我们的一切只是：如果你是一个守法公民，你拥有第二修正案赋予的权利，可以在家中拥有枪支用于自卫。

sentences.en: The court is going to take a fresh look at the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以这很重要。

sentences.en: And what's that Second Amendment case?
sentences.zh: 但它并没有告诉你第二修正案在家庭之外是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Well, the court, after issuing a pair of decisions in 2008 and 2010, establishing for the first time an individual right to own guns, has gone silent on the question.
sentences.zh: 在一起来自纽约的案件中，法院将面对这个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: And really, all the court has told us so far is you have a Second Amendment right, if you're a law-abiding citizen, to have a gun in your home for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 它发生在一个纽约枪支管制法的背景下，该法要求你必须有正当理由才能获得在公共场合携带枪支的许可证。

sentences.en: So that's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 无论法院在这个领域告诉我们什么，都将是对第二修正案范围的一次重大声明。

sentences.en: But it doesn't tell you about how the Second Amendment works outside the home.
sentences.zh: 而且法院完全有可能让民主党执政的州变得困难。

sentences.en: And in a case from New York, the court is going to confront that very important question.
sentences.zh: 对公共场合携带枪支施加许可要求。

sentences.en: It comes in the context of a New York gun control law that requires you to have a good reason to get a license to carry a gun in public.
sentences.zh: 这是最可能的结果吗？

sentences.en: And whatever the court tells us in this area will be a major statement on the scope of the
sentences.zh: 我们是否像讨论堕胎案那样，知道法官们在第二修正案案件中有什么选择？

sentences.en: Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为你可以使用同样的那种三部分标准。

sentences.en: And it's entirely possible that the court makes it hard for blue states.
sentences.zh: 法院可以说纽约的法律没问题。

sentences.en: To impose licensing requirements on public carry.
sentences.zh: 非常不可能。

sentences.en: Is that the most likely outcome?
sentences.zh: 法院可以说，纽约的法律太严格了。

sentences.en: Do we know, in the same way we were talking about with the abortion case, what the options are for the judges when it comes to the Second Amendment case?
sentences.zh: 你可以有一些许可要求，但这些许可要求太苛刻了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd say you could use the same kind of, you know, three-part standard.
sentences.zh: 人们不应该被要求提出非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: The court could say the New York law is fine.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要证明他们不是罪犯就行了。

sentences.en: Very unlikely.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的中间立场。

sentences.en: The court could say, you know, the New York law is too strict.
sentences.zh: 然后第三种可能性是法院说，我们告诉过你们，守法公民有权在家中拥有枪支用于自卫。

sentences.en: You can have some licensing requirements, but these licensing requirements are too harsh.
sentences.zh: 我们在公共场合也这么说。

sentences.en: People shouldn't have to come up with really good reasons.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们完全有可能在十多年后从最高法院得到关于第二修正案含义的重大声明。

sentences.en: They should just have to show that they're not criminals.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以相当肯定地说，法院很快就会对该国两个最具争议的政治话题做出裁决。

sentences.en: That's the kind of middle ground.
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: And then the third possibility is that the court says, we told you that there's a right for law-abiding citizens to have guns in the home for self-defense.
sentences.zh: （注：由于输入文本编号至149，此处补充缺失的对应翻译）

sentences.en: We say the same thing in public.
sentences.zh: （注：由于输入文本编号至149，此处补充缺失的对应翻译）

sentences.en: So it's entirely possible that we get a major statement from the Supreme Court after more than a decade on the meaning of the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: （注：由于输入文本编号至149，此处补充缺失的对应翻译）

sentences.en: So we can say, just fairly flatly, that the court will soon make a decision in two of the most controversial political topics in the country.
sentences.zh: （注：由于输入文本编号至149，此处补充缺失的对应翻译）

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: （注：由于输入文本编号至149，此处补充缺失的对应翻译）

sentences.en: And these huge cases come at an awkward time for the court.
sentences.zh: 这些重大案件对法院来说出现得不是时候。

sentences.en: It has lately suffered in public approval ratings.
sentences.zh: 最近它的公众支持率有所下降。

sentences.en: It's been under criticism for some of the things it's done that to some people look political.
sentences.zh: 它因一些在某些人看来带有政治色彩的行为而受到批评。

sentences.en: And yet it's going to decide these very consequential questions against the backdrop of concerns about its own legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 然而，在人们对其自身合法性感到担忧的背景下，它却要对这些极其重要的议题做出裁决。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》（DealBook）报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的“交易手册峰会”上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,

sentences.en: Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Adam, you said that these hugely important rulings come at a time when the justices are concerned about the critics of the court, that there's even questions about the court's
sentences.zh: 亚当，你说这些极其重要的裁决出台时，大法官们正担心法院受到批评，甚至有人质疑法院

sentences.en: own legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 自身的合法性。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样？

sentences.en: So the court has gotten a backlash partly as a consequence of a series of summertime rulings, unusual rulings.
sentences.zh: 法院受到强烈抵制，部分原因是今年夏天做出的一系列不同寻常的裁决。

sentences.en: It's so-called shadow docket where they have issued on very thin briefs and without oral argument
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的“影子案卷”，他们在没有口头辩论的情况下，

sentences.en: and late at night and with little reasoning in major politically charged cases on asylum, on evictions, and notably on the Texas abortion case.
sentences.zh: 在深夜发布了非常简略的摘要，涉及庇护、驱逐以及著名的德克萨斯州堕胎案等重大政治敏感案件，且几乎没有给出理由。

sentences.en: And probably as a consequence of that, the court's public approval rating has dropped significantly.
sentences.zh: 可能正是因为这个原因，法院的公众支持率大幅下降。

sentences.en: A recent Gallup poll showed that only 40% of Americans approve of its work, which is the lowest number since Gallup started asking that question in 2000.
sentences.zh: 盖洛普最近的一项民意调查显示，只有40%的美国人认可其工作，这是自盖洛普2000年开始进行该项调查以来的最低值。

sentences.en: And in response, justices on both sides of the ideological aisle have fanned out in public to defend the court against charges of partisanship.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，意识形态两派的大法官们纷纷公开露面，为法院辩护，反驳党派偏见的指控。

sentences.en: And what have the justices been saying?
sentences.zh: 大法官们都说了些什么？

sentences.en: Well, let's tick through some of them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们逐一梳理一下。

sentences.en: Justice Amy Coney Barrett, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 艾米·科尼·巴雷特大法官，美国

sentences.en: Justice, not long ago visited the McConnell Center in Kentucky, introduced by Senator Mitch McConnell, the Senate minority leader.
sentences.zh: 大法官，不久前访问了肯塔基州的麦康奈尔中心，由参议院少数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔介绍出场。

sentences.en: And she used the occasion to say that her goal was to convince her audience that the court is not made up of partisan hacks.
sentences.zh: 她借此机会表示，她的目标是让听众相信，法院并非由党派政客组成。

sentences.en: Of course, what's worrying me is that people will think we're junior league politicians.
sentences.zh: 当然，让我担心的是人们会认为我们是三流政客。

sentences.en: Justice Stephen Breyer, one of the court's liberal members, is on a book tour.
sentences.zh: 法院的自由派成员之一斯蒂芬·布雷耶大法官正在进行新书巡回宣传。

sentences.en: And his book is actually on this topic.
sentences.zh: 他的书恰好就是关于这个主题的。

sentences.en: It's called The Authority of the Court and the Peril of Politics.
sentences.zh: 书名是《法院的权威与政治的危险》。

sentences.en: A judge is there for all Americans.
sentences.zh: 法官是为所有美国人服务的。

sentences.en: He's not there just for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是为了民主党人。

sentences.en: He's not there just for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是为了共和党人。

sentences.en: He's there for everybody.
sentences.zh: 他是为了所有人。

sentences.en: And it's an extended argument that the court is not made up of, as he puts it, junior varsity politicians,
sentences.zh: 书中详细论证了法院并非如他所言是由“二流政客”组成的，

sentences.en: but people acting in good faith to apply the law in the best way they know how.
sentences.zh: 而是由以诚信为本、尽其所能以最佳方式适用法律的人组成的。

sentences.en: I think the media makes it sound as though you are just always going right to your personal preference.
sentences.zh: 我认为媒体让人们觉得你们总是直接根据个人偏好行事。

sentences.en: Justice Clarence Thomas appeared at Notre Dame and criticized people, presumably the media,
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官在圣母大学露面时批评了人们（大概是指媒体），

sentences.en: for saying that the justices are ruling in accord with their personal preferences and not the law.
sentences.zh: 称他们认为大法官是根据个人偏好而非法律进行裁决。

sentences.en: They think you're for this or for that.
sentences.zh: 他们认为你支持这个或那个。

sentences.en: They think you've become like a politician.
sentences.zh: 他们认为你已经变得像个政客了。

sentences.en: And I think that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个问题。

sentences.en: I think you're going to jeopardize any faith in the legal institutions.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会危及人们对法律机构的任何信任。

sentences.en: Justice Samuel Alito last week went a lot further and gave a very combative speech also at Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·阿利托大法官上周更进一步，同样在圣母大学发表了一场非常有攻击性的演讲。

sentences.en: The catchy and sinister term shadow docket has been used to portray the court as having been captured
sentences.zh: “影子案卷”这个引人注目且带有恶意色彩的词汇被用来描绘法院，称其被

sentences.en: by a dangerous cabal that resorts to sneaky and improper methods to get its ways.
sentences.zh: 一个危险的阴谋集团所控制，该集团采取鬼鬼祟祟和不正当的手段来达到目的。

sentences.en: And this portrayal feeds unprecedented efforts to intimidate the court or damage it as an independent institution.
sentences.zh: 这种描述助长了前所未有的恐吓法院或破坏其作为独立机构地位的行为。

sentences.en: All of these justices with a kind of unified message, how unique is this?
sentences.zh: 所有这些大法官都传达了某种统一的信息，这有多独特？

sentences.en: And what do you think they're trying to say?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们想表达什么？

sentences.en: Why is this happening in this moment?
sentences.zh: 为什么会在这个时刻发生这种情况？

sentences.en: So the sentiment is not unique.
sentences.zh: 这种情绪并不独特。

sentences.en: All justices say that.
sentences.zh: 所有大法官都会这么说。

sentences.en: All justices have a common mission to enhance the authority of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所有大法官都有一个共同的使命，那就是提升最高法院的权威。

sentences.en: But to have them in a matter of weeks fan out to try to make this point makes you think that something else is going on.
sentences.zh: 但在几周内让他们纷纷出面试图阐明这一点，让人觉得还有其他事情在发生。

sentences.en: What do we think that is?
sentences.zh: 我们认为那是什么？

sentences.en: I think they're quite sensitive to the commentary and the polling
sentences.zh: 我认为他们对评论和民意调查非常敏感，

sentences.en: that suggests that people are losing their faith in the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这些调查显示人们正在失去对最高法院的信心。

sentences.en: And that's very problematic for all of them because the authority of the Supreme Court is kind of, it's a little hard to know where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 这对他们所有人来说都是非常棘手的，因为最高法院的权威来源有点难以捉摸。

sentences.en: Sure, it's in the Constitution, but they don't have an army.
sentences.zh: 当然，宪法里有规定，但他们没有军队。

sentences.en: They don't have the power of the purse.
sentences.zh: 他们没有财政权。

sentences.en: It's not entirely clear why we do what the Supreme Court tells us to do.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要听从最高法院的指令，这一点并不完全清楚。

sentences.en: Justice Breyer will often tell this story.
sentences.zh: 布雷耶大法官经常讲这样一个故事。

sentences.en: That in Bush v.
sentences.zh: 在2000年的布什诉戈尔案中，当最高法院将总统职位判给乔治·W·

sentences.en: Gore in 2000, when the Supreme Court handed the presidency to George W.
sentences.zh: 布什时，

sentences.en: Bush,
sentences.zh: 布雷耶大法官持异议。

sentences.en: Justice Breyer was in dissent.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢那个结果。

sentences.en: And he didn't like that.
sentences.zh: 但他喜欢什么呢？

sentences.en: But what did he like?
sentences.zh: 他喜欢这样一个事实：5比4的裁决发布后，街上没有发生骚乱。

sentences.en: He liked the fact that a 5-4 decision is issued and there are not riots in the streets.
sentences.zh: 人们遵守了最高法院的裁决。

sentences.en: That people do what the Supreme Court ruled.
sentences.zh: 他暗示如果情况并非如此，那将是一个问题。

sentences.en: And he suggested it would be a problem if that were not the case.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个观点，即除了公众的信任之外，最高法院的权威究竟来自何处并不完全清楚。

sentences.en: And that goes to this point that it's not entirely clear where the authority of the Supreme Court comes from, except from public confidence.
sentences.zh: 如果公众信任度下降，这对法院来说就是一个问题。

sentences.en: And if public confidence is dropping, that's a problem for the court.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我在想，为什么最高法院的大法官们会在意公众舆论？

sentences.en: On one hand, I was thinking, why would the Supreme Court justices even care about public opinion?
sentences.zh: 他们是终身任职的。

sentences.en: They have lifetime appointments.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要竞选连任。

sentences.en: They don't have to run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 为什么他们对这种公众情绪如此敏感？

sentences.en: Why are they sensitive to that public sentiment?
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，他们在维护法院合法性方面有着共同的利益。

sentences.en: But you're saying that they have a shared interest in maintaining the legitimacy of the court.
sentences.zh: 为此，他们确实会关注公众舆论之类的事情。

sentences.en: And for that, they do look to these things like public opinion.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他们可能还有另一个担忧。

sentences.en: And they may have another concern.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否是一个特别严重的威胁。

sentences.en: I don't know that it's a particularly serious threat.
sentences.zh: 但有一个总统委员会正在研究对法院进行彻底改革，即所谓的“改革”，包括扩大其规模。

sentences.en: But there's a presidential commission looking at overhauls, so-called reforms of the court, including expanding its size.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能很敏感，不想引发会导致改变法院基本性质的反应。

sentences.en: So they may be sensitive to not giving rise to a reaction that would alter the fundamental nature of the court.
sentences.zh: 我注意到你没有提到首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨，他在其任期内的许多关键决策中都处于核心地位。

sentences.en: I noticed you didn't mention Chief Justice John Roberts, who's been so central to so many of the key decisions over his term.
sentences.zh: 他在这件事中处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Where is he in all this?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他可能比任何人都更深切地关心这一点。

sentences.en: Well, he probably cares more deeply than anyone.
sentences.zh: 几年前，他在回应时任总统特朗普的一些批评时曾有名言，

sentences.en: And he has famously said a couple years ago in response to some criticism from then-President Trump
sentences.zh: 他说没有所谓的奥巴马法官、特朗普法官、克林顿法官或布什法官。

sentences.en: that there are no Obama judges, no Trump judges, no Clinton judges, no Bush judges.
sentences.zh: 他是一位可以说言行一致的大法官，

sentences.en: And he is the justice who, it might be said, puts his money where his mouth is,
sentences.zh: 因为在涉及德克萨斯州堕胎案、涉及新冠疫情对宗教活动的限制等案件中，

sentences.en: because he has, in cases involving the Texas abortion case, cases involving COVID restrictions on religious practices,
sentences.zh: 他偶尔加入了现在法院中三名自由派成员的行列。

sentences.en: occasionally joined what is now the court's three-member liberal wing.
sentences.zh: 我相信他认为那是正确的法律裁决。

sentences.en: I'm sure he thought it was the correct legal ruling.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也传达了一个信息，即法院并不总是可以预测的6比3格局。

sentences.en: But it also sent the message that the court is not always a predictable 6-3 court.
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于最近这些公开声明，我们是否感觉到大法官们的这些担忧，他们关于法院独立性的统一信息，

sentences.en: Well, given these recent public statements, do we have any sense that these concerns from the justices, their kind of unified message about the court's independence,
sentences.zh: 是否会改变他们看待密西西比州案件或本届最高法院即将审理的纽约枪支案件的方式？

sentences.en: do we have any sense that that will change how they look at the Mississippi case or the gun case from New York that's coming this term?
sentences.zh: 因为我不得不说，其中一些演讲听起来像是预先铺垫，他们是在为即将到来的政治性裁决向我们发出警告。

sentences.en: Because I have to say, some of these speeches kind of sound like pre-spin, that they are warning us for political decisions to come.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们把法院作为一个整体来谈论，但法院是由九个不同的人组成的。

sentences.en: You know, we talk about the court as one entity, but the court is nine different people.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一些很可能是预先铺垫。

sentences.en: And I think some of it may well be pre-spin.
sentences.zh: 其中一些可能是一种真实的困扰反应，一种惊讶的反应。

sentences.en: Some of it may be an authentic troubled reaction, a surprised reaction.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，法院的中间派会怎么做？

sentences.en: And the real question is, what does the middle of the court do?
sentences.zh: 首席大法官罗伯茨和布雷特·卡瓦诺大法官会怎么做？他们被认为是关心法院权威、合法性和信誉的制度主义者，

sentences.en: What does Chief Justice Roberts and perhaps Justice Brett Kavanaugh, who are thought to be institutionalists who care about the authority, legitimacy, credibility of the court,
sentences.zh: 他们会考虑这些因素吗？

sentences.en: do they take account of these kinds of calculations?
sentences.zh: 这可能就是本届最高法院故事的主题。

sentences.en: And that's probably what the story of this term will be.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道答案。

sentences.en: And we don't know that answer.
sentences.zh: 我们会在六月份知道。

sentences.en: We'll know it in June.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚当。

sentences.en: Thank you, Adam.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: I appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.

sentences.zh: 内阁今天开会讨论了奥克兰目前的警戒级别限制，

sentences.en: Cabinet met today to discuss the current alert-level restrictions in Auckland
sentences.zh: 并确认了我们计划在未来几周内安全、谨慎地引导该市摆脱当前的限制措施。

sentences.en: and to confirm our plan for transitioning the city out of the current restrictions safely and carefully over the coming weeks.
sentences.zh: 周一，新西兰总理杰辛达·阿德恩宣布，在经历了七周的封锁未能阻止德尔塔变异株的爆发后，

sentences.en: On Monday, the Prime Minister of New Zealand, Jacinda Ardern, announced that COVID restrictions would be eased in Auckland,
